an endogenous inhibitor for the ADP‐ ribosylation reaction of G‐protein(s), as catalyzed pertussis toxin, is present in rat tissues.
we found a protein that inhibits ADP‐ribosylylation of G proteins in rat liver.
an endogenous inhibitor for pertussis toxin‐catalyzed ADP ribosylation of (α) G‐protein (s) exists in the liver membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of an inhibitor of the ADPR‐G‐protein reaction in rat liver.
the endogenous inhibitors of the ADP ‐ ribosylation reaction of G‐ protein(s) catalyzed by the pertussis toxin.
the endogenous inhibitor of pertussis‐toxin‐catalyzed (a) GTP‐binding protein(s) ADP‐ribosylylation reaction in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endogenous inhibitor of pertussis‐ADP‐ribosyltransferase is present in the liver, but not in the brain.

the inhibitor of pertussis ADP ribosylation is a GTP‐binding protein, which is a member of a family of GTP‐binding proteins that includes the α‐subunit of the G‐proteins that mediate the actions of many hormones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ADP‐ribo‐sylation of (a) Gi protein(s) is inhibited by the endogenous inhibitors in the membrane fraction of the liver and the brain, and that the endogenous inhibitors are not the same as the inhibitors of the ADP-ribosylation of GTP binding proteins as catalyzed b y cholera toxin.
the ADP‐ribo‐syltransferase activity of pertussis and/or cholera toxin is not only regulated by the amount of G‐protein but is also controlled by the endogenous inhibitor of ADP‐ribosy­lation.

there are endogenous inhibitors of the pertussis toxin‐catalyzed ADP‐ribosyation of G proteins in the membrane extract from rat liver.
